text:
alex: Heads-up — we're updating the private deployment KMS integration for the EU on-prem pilot. Need to confirm RBAC changes + fallback behaviour if external KMS (customer HSM) becomes unreachable.

maria: What exactly is the failure scenario we want to tolerate? complete KMS outage, network partition, or auth failure?

sam: All of the above. Plus a realistic onprem: intermittent TLS handshake drops, and the keystore proxy backpressure when SIEM shipper spikes.

jen: My checklist: 1) ensure service-accounts can't call Decrypt except via the keystore-shim. 2) keep a wrapped-key cache with strict TTL. 3) audit log every unwrap and fallback.

phil: Agree on wrapped-key cache. Important: cache must be encrypted and marked read-only after N minutes to avoid silent rewraps. Also we must treat cached keys as high-sensitivity — restrict access to sysadmins and keystore component only.

alex: Proposed flow: on decrypt request -> authz check (k8s SA annotation) -> call keystore-shim which requests key material from external KMS. If KMS times out, keystore-shim attempts unwrap from local wrapped-key cache (TTL 24h default, configurable). If cache miss -> fail-open? no. Fail-closed but with degraded read-only inference mode.

maria: Degraded read-only inference mode = serve cached model artifacts only, deny new model loads and any write path that would call KMS. We need explicit audit markers so ops can see "mode=degraded-kms" for every request.

sam: How do we prevent replay if attacker steals wrapped cache? We need additional MAC tied to node identity. Suggest node signs unwrap attempts with node key and the shim performs attestation check against control-plane.

jen: For attestation: we can use mTLS client cert plus a short-lived node identity token issued by control plane (ttl=5m). That plus per-node HSM protected private keys reduces replay risk.

phil: Network policy notes: keystore-shim must only egress to (1) customer-KMS endpoints over TLS 443, (2) control-plane attestation API port 8443, and (3) SIEM/shipper endpoint for audit logs. No other egress allowed. Use egress policies with dest CIDRs and SNI enforcement where possible.

alex: On audit logging: central requirement is immutable tamper-evident records for unwrap/decrypt and fallback events. We'll ship events to auditsvc with fields: event, node_id, shim_version, mode, reason, request_id. Retention 1y hot, 5y cold (enterprise).

auditsvc: +1. We'll include HMAC of the event blob using a rotation-aware signing key. Logs will be accepted only from keystore-shim with mTLS cert pinned in control plane.

maria: Incident response scenario: if we detect unusual unwrap rate from a single node (threshold > 100 unwraps/min) and simultaneous KMS timeouts, trigger automated isolation: cordon node, rotate the node ephemeral key, and revoke its attestation token. Ops to investigate.

sam: Can we instrument a lightweight in-shim circuit-breaker? if downstream KMS RTT > 2s for 10s -> open circuit for 60s and switch to cache-only mode, emit alert to #eng-oncall and to sec-oncall-bot.

jen: For RBAC change plan: create a new k8s ClusterRole "keystore-unwrapper" bound to a dedicated ServiceAccount per namespace. Deny system:authenticated any direct access to decrypt endpoints. We'll prepare a migration job that audits current callers for 2 weeks before enforcement.

phil: Quick config snippet for netpol egress (example):
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: keystore-egress
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: keystore-shim
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.8.99.0/24 # control plane
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8443
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          infra: external-apis
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

alex: Nice. Ops action items: 1) write migration plan for RBAC change + 2-week audit window. 2) implement wrapped-key cache with node-bound MAC. 3) add circuit-breaker + alerting. 4) lock down netpol egress rules. 5) add audit HMAC signing and SIEM ingestion.

maria: I'll own 1 & 4. Sam will own 2 & 3. Jen will own 5 and coordinate retention SLAs.

sam: I'll spin up a PoC branch for the cache with optional FIPS-compatible crypto layer.

phil: One more: include a playbook snippet for incident response in case of suspected key compromise. Steps: revoke node attestation, rotate wrapped cache, require re-attestation, run forensic dump of unwrap events between t-24h and now.

sec-oncall-bot: Incident playbook link https://redwood-internal/policies/priv-kms-incident (pinned). Use reaction :eyes: to ack.

alex: Thanks all — I'll open CL with RBAC manifests and the migration audit query. Expect PR by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
